$comment: The deck for the site's shared synthetic Eclipse model. This file holds only what a human
chose: dimensions, well locations and trajectories, controls, events, and the trend
parameters the property distributions are drawn from. Every bulky numeric array is
generated deterministically from the seed below by wwwroot/js/demos/model.js.
See docs/DEMO-MODEL.md for the data sheet and docs/ADR-002-interactive-demos.md for why.
This model is entirely synthetic. It is not derived from any customer dataset.

grid.$comment: Inactive cells: small clusters at the periphery of the top layer only.

layerTrends.$comment: Per-layer means. PERMX is drawn lognormally about permMean; PERMZ = 0.1 x PERMX.

fluids.$comment: Metric. Pressures barsa, Bo/Bw rm3/sm3, Rs sm3/sm3, viscosity cP, ct 1/bar.
$comment2: A simple steady-state aquifer: influx rate = aquiferStrength x (initial - current)
pressure. Without it the tank depletes far faster than any real field, because a fixed
BHP with rising water cut roughly doubles liquid offtake over field life.
Injection is deliberately set to a voidage replacement ratio of roughly 0.6, with the
aquifer making up the balance. A VRR near 1.0 holds pressure almost flat, which is good
field management but leaves FPR a horizontal line and the producing gas/oil ratio pinned
at Rs — two of the more instructive curves reduced to nothing.
Wells. i/j are 1-based Eclipse indices. 'deviation' gives the cumulative [di, dj] offset
at each of the 10 layers; a straight vertical well omits it. Completions are derived as
every active cell the track passes through, so a track crossing an inactive top-layer
cluster simply has no perforation in layer 1.
$comment3: i/j deliberately NOT on two dead-even rows: a perfectly uniform well pattern read as an
obvious pilot/test grid rather than a real field layout. Nudged by a cell or two each,
keeping the same rough two-line drive pattern (producers upper, injectors lower) real field
layouts often share, and kept clear of the inactive top-layer clusters below (their j-range
is 1-3/19-21; every well here sits well outside that).

$comment: targetInitialOilRate calibrates the productivity indices: the per-well J values are
derived from kh over each well's completions, then scaled together so the field opens at
this rate. Everything after that is consequence, not tuning.
Shut-ins are NOT dated here. Prod_3 and Prod_5 carry an economic water-cut limit, as
WECON would apply it per well, and each shuts on the first month its own water cut
reaches the limit. The date is therefore a result of the model, so the cause of the
shut-in is genuinely visible on the same plot rather than arranged to look that way.
rampMonths applies to every injector at startup.
Observed (history) vectors are the simulated series plus bias and coarser noise, and are
deliberately sparse and partly stale — a proportion of months are missing and a
proportion repeat the previous reading. Without that, 'Show Observed Data' and 'Hide
Repeated Observed Data' would demonstrate nothing.
